items.summary: Financial recommendation: hold new spend, monetization expansion, and new queue actions; preserve only existing bounded reversible work until measurement closes. Known facts: AI usage cost $759.78 for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-23 across 4,529 calls; Amazon reported 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission for 2026-09-21, with $0 site-attributed income and all $4.92 explicitly unattributed. Therefore revenue claims, site-level contribution margin, ROI, CAC, payback, profitability, and forecasts are unsupported. A simple $4.92 minus $759.78 comparison is not a valid margin because the periods, attribution, and cost scopes do not match. Cost-to-learn is also not calculable: three improvements await measurement, zero outcomes are proven, and AI cost is not mapped to experiment, site, or causal lift. Minimum measurement: daily site/content identifiers connecting AI and infrastructure costs, analytics sessions and conversion events, affiliate clicks, orders, shipped items, commissions, and experiment exposure/control with a defined measurement window. Direct infrastructure spend, fixed costs, labor cost, and budget limits are unavailable, so budget exposure cannot be quantified. Recommendation remains to complete existing measurement gates, avoid duplicate work, and reject vanity metrics such as impressions, clicks, calls, and conversions as financial proof without attributable revenue and incremental lift.

CFO review: retain the private-preview gate. No revenue or margin claim should be made until source rights, affiliate attribution, direct-cost inputs, and measurement controls are complete. No budget, billing, banking, contract, credential, or production action is recommended. The minimum finance gate is a reconciled report tying traffic, affiliate events, orders, shipped items, commission, AI cost, infrastructure cost, and experiment exposure to site and content identifiers.
